page.layout: One page of text, one column; handwritten marks in the left margin; show-through of the facing page at the right edge (not transcribed). Running head at top with page number left.

main_text.p: ubicunq; in theatris effet expofita, statim & men tes & oculi spectatorum admiratione incredibili stupescerent. Huc congruit & descriptio Cico-niarum, quæ ab Aristophane non insuauiter recitatur. Vtinam nos singuli hoc insigne exemplum imitaremur, & simili pietate erga sanctissimam nostram parentem Ecclesiam, nunc mœstã & humanis præsidijs orbatam, affecti essemus, & no-stra gratitudine omnibus officijs ostenderemus.
main_text.head: INGRATITVDO ERGA parentes, cognatos & præceptores.
main_text.p: Mahometus, qui cepit Constantinopolim interfecit duos fratres paruulos, & alterum paruulum in sinu matris.

Selinus pater huius Solimanni, interfecit & patrem fugientem, & fratrem, & in eo ipso loco ubi pater est interfectus, iuxta Baiarum ulcere sæuissimo diuinitùs inflicto mortuus est. Locus ostenditur in Macedoniam iter facientibus per Hungariam.
main_text.head: COLL.
main_text.p: Aristoteles in nono libro de Anima scribit, cuculum propter impietatem, quam in ipso insignem esse compertum est, non facere proprium nidum, nec suos pullos excludere, sed deponere ouâ

page.notes: Handwritten annotations in the left margin ("reum Sing", "y/rere", and a manicule) are manuscript marks, not printed text, and are not transcribed. A worm-hole/stain near "ulcere" and a blot at "Baiarum" are damage. The catchword "ouâ" is read from the last line's end and may be a catchword rather than line-end text. Some letters in the running head and body are uncertain due to the scan's low contrast.
